title: Why does everything keep getting more expensive?
tension: Your money is quietly dying, and that is not a malfunction, it is the design. The ₹100 a parent saved in 2012 buys about ₹51 of the same things today; ₹100 from 1960 buys almost nothing. Inflation is the slow tax nobody votes for, and yet a little of it is exactly what the country's central bank is trying to produce, because the alternative is worse. The real question is never whether prices rise, but how fast, who decides, and who gets hurt while it happens.
teachingGoal: Give a reader with no economics a true working grasp of inflation: what it is, how much the rupee has actually eroded, why prices rise at all, why a little inflation is deliberately targeted rather than zero, who controls the pace (the RBI, its 4% target, the repo rate), and how India's inflation compares with the world. They should finish able to read an inflation headline and understand what it is doing to them.
sectionArc: What is inflation, in one breath? (a sustained, general rise in prices; the ₹100-from-2012 erosion; today's CPI rate)
How much has the rupee actually shrunk? (the long view: price level since 1960, how many times prices have risen, ₹100 from 1960 today; average inflation by decade)

Why do prices rise at all, and is it bad? (too much money chasing too few goods; demand-pull vs cost-push, in plain terms; why mild inflation is healthier than zero, and why falling prices, deflation, are worse)
Who decides how fast prices rise? (the RBI's job; the 4% target and the tolerance band; the repo rate as the brake and accelerator)
Is India's inflation high or low by world standards? (CPI against the US, China, Brazil; India's rate in context; how a country tames hyperinflation)
Why does the official number so often feel wrong? (it is an average of a fixed basket that may not be yours; a pointer to the deeper entries)
So what does inflation actually do to you, and what can you do about it? (why cash under the mattress loses; the everyday logic behind gold and property; read it, do not ignore it)
mustTeach: inflation is a sustained, general rise in the overall price level, which lowers what each rupee buys
India's rupee has eroded dramatically over decades: prices today are many times their 1960 level
a little, steady inflation is deliberately targeted because deflation (falling prices) can be more damaging
the RBI controls the pace mainly through the policy repo rate, aiming at a 4% CPI target within a 2-6% band
inflation rates vary hugely across countries, and the official figure is an average that hides individual experience
featureNumbers: How many times prices have risen since 1960, latest

contextCards.fact: In 2016 India adopted a formal flexible inflation-targeting framework. The Finance Act amended the RBI Act to make price stability the primary goal of monetary policy, set a Consumer Price Index inflation target of 4 percent with a tolerance band of 2 to 6 percent, and created a six-member Monetary Policy Committee (three from the RBI, including the Governor as chair, and three appointed by the government) to set the policy repo rate to hit it.
contextCards.source: Finance Act 2016 / RBI Act amendment; RBI Monetary Policy Committee (verified, standard)

contextCards.fact: Central banks deliberately aim for low, steady inflation (commonly 2 to 4 percent) rather than zero. Mild inflation greases the economy, letting wages and prices adjust, and keeps a safe distance from deflation, a sustained fall in prices that can make people delay spending, squeeze borrowers, and deepen downturns. Runaway inflation is destructive, but so is its opposite.
